cards.question: What are the West zones of the lung?
cards.answer: Zone 1 (apex) — alveolar pressure > arterial > venous; no flow (alveolar dead space). Zone 2 — arterial > alveolar > venous; flow driven by arterial − alveolar pressure ('waterfall'). Zone 3 (base) — arterial > venous > alveolar; flow driven by arterial − venous (continuous). Zone 1 normally absent but appears with hypotension, PEEP overshoot, or PE.

cards.question: Define shunt and V/Q mismatch, and how do their responses to supplemental oxygen differ?
cards.answer: Shunt — perfused but not ventilated (V/Q = 0); blood bypasses gas exchange entirely (pneumonia, atelectasis, ARDS, intracardiac). Shunted blood bypasses ventilated alveoli, so supplemental oxygen has limited effect on it. V/Q mismatch — areas of low V/Q ratio; partial gas exchange occurs; low-V/Q units generally respond better to supplemental oxygen than true shunt. The whole-arterial response depends on the shunt fraction, mixed venous O₂ content and the ventilated units; neither the oxygen response nor a fixed 30% threshold alone determines treatment.

cards.question: What is hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction and why does it matter for one-lung ventilation?
cards.answer: HPV — pulmonary arteriolar constriction in response to low alveolar O₂; diverts blood from poorly ventilated alveoli to better-ventilated regions, reducing shunt. Volatile anaesthetics ≥1 MAC blunt HPV (~20 % attenuation). For one-lung ventilation during thoracic surgery, TIVA preserves HPV better and may improve oxygenation; CPAP to the non-ventilated lung or PEEP to the dependent lung are rescue strategies.
